question: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) is an otological emergency and should be treated with systemic corticosteroids within 72 hours of onset to maximise recovery.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. SSNHL is an otological emergency. A patient who wakes up deaf in one ear must be seen urgently. High-dose oral prednisolone (or intratympanic steroids) within 72 hours is the evidence-based treatment; waiting wastes the window for recovery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. SSNHL (loss of 30 dB or more across 3 consecutive frequencies over 72 hours) is an emergency. Systemic (and/or intratympanic) corticosteroids within 72 hours of onset are the mainstay of treatment. Delay significantly reduces the chance of hearing recovery.
